journey.name: wear quickpay on app start
journey.description:
A payment link that starts the app is paid under QuickPay too, although the last import of the phone's settings is too old by then: the send waits a moment for the import and the rates that the start brings, and then goes out without the review and the hold. Emulator, or a physical watch that stays on the wrist and unlocked.
Precondition: run quickpay-skips-hold.xml first, so the watch's last import has QuickPay on with Default Unit Bitcoin, Denomination Modern and Local Currency USD, which the amount below counts on, and change nothing on the phone since. Watch: the wallet of quickpay-skips-hold.xml on the local ./spark stack with at least 2 000 sats and a network on which the balance comes back within 20 s of a start. A wallet that needs more than 30 s shows the review and the hold instead, which is as designed and fails this journey. So does a watch that locked during the 16 minutes: KEYCODE_WAKEUP lights the screen and unlocks nothing, and QuickPay never pays on a locked watch. Use the emulator, which has no lock, or keep a physical watch on the wrist and unlocked for the whole wait.

actions.action: Wait 16 minutes, as 16 waits of 1 minute and not one long sleep, touching nothing: the last import is then too old for QuickPay
Run `../bitkit-docker/spark invoice 200` and note the BOLT11 invoice it prints as <invoice>
Run `adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "lightning:<invoice>" to.bitkit.dev`, which starts the app
Wait up to 40 s until "WatchSendSent" is listed, touching nothing
Verify `adb logcat -d -s BitkitWear` lists "Imported the phone's settings"
Verify `adb logcat -d -s BitkitWear` lists "Skipped the hold to pay under QuickPay"
